We have template details. The retro_smarts_template is:

'[C:8]-[C@@H;D3;+0:9](-[C@H;D3;+0:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12])-[C@;H0;D4;+0:2](-[C:1])(-[OH;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])-[F;D1;H0:7]>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7]).[C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]'

So forward reaction: product side is left? Actually retro_smarts_template shows reactants -> products? Usually retro template is product->reactants. Here retro_smarts_template: left side is product? It shows a complex scaffold with many atoms, then >> product side: a carbonyl and an alkene fragment. So retrosynthetic step: target (complex) can be disconnected into two fragments: a carbonyl fragment (C:1 - C:2(=O) - C:4(F3) etc) and an alkene fragment (C:8=CH-...). The target is the left side (the complex). So applying this template retrosynthetically to target should give two precursors: a carbonyl fragment (maybe a trifluoromethyl ketone) and an alkene fragment (maybe a styrene-like). The target SMILES is:

[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We need to map atoms to template. The template mapping shows product side: [CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] . That seems similar to our target but with CH3 at C1? Our target has [CH2]=[C]... not CH3. The template expects a CH3 attached to C1? Actually mapped_rxn shows product side: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])>>([...]) So product is a molecule with CH3 attached to C2? Wait.

Our target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

In template, the left side (reactant) is a more complex: [C:8]-[C@@H:9]... etc. The right side (product) is two fragments: a carbonyl fragment and an alkene fragment.

Thus applying retro template to target should give two fragments: fragment A: [C:1]-[C](=O)-[C](F)(F)F (a trifluoroacetyl group attached to something). Fragment B: [C:8]/[CH]=[C]... (an alkene with aromatic). Let's apply apply_template again but maybe need to use canonical_smarts_template? The tool apply_template uses the template ID; earlier it returned empty because maybe the target didn't match due to atom mapping differences. But we have the mapped_rxn which shows the product side matches our target? The mapped_rxn shows product side: ([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]) . Our target has CH2 at position 1 not CH3. So maybe we need to adjust? Could be that the template expects a methyl group attached to the alkene carbon (C1). Our target has CH2 (i.e., a terminal alkene). So maybe we need to add a methyl group as a protecting group? But requirement is to use the template; maybe we can propose a precursor that has a methyl group which after some step (e.g., demethylation) yields the target. But we need only one reaction using this template. The route must have at least 1 reaction, using template 1914384. So we can propose that the target is formed by a retro step that splits into two fragments: a trifluoroacetyl fragment and a styrene-like fragment with a methyl group. Then we can propose that the methyl group is removed later? But we only need one reaction.

Thus we can propose the retrosynthetic step: target -> precursor1 (trifluoroacetyl ketone) + precursor2 (methyl-substituted alkene). Provide SMILES for each.

Let's derive precursor SMILES.

Fragment A (carbonyl fragment): According to template, it's [C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4](-[F;D1;H0:5])(-[F;D1;H0:6])(-[F;D1;H0:7])

Mapping: C1 is attached to C2 (which is carbonyl). C2 is carbonyl carbon attached to O. C4 is CF3 group attached to C2? Actually C4 is the carbon bearing three Fs. So the fragment is something like R-CO-CF3 where R is C1 (maybe a methyl). In our target, C1 is CH3? The mapped_rxn shows CH3 attached to C2. So fragment A is CH3-CO-CF3 (i.e., trifluoroacetone? Actually CH3-CO-CF3 is 1,1,1-trifluoro-2-propanone, also called trifluoroacetone). SMILES: CC(=O)C(F)(F)F . That's CH3-CO-CF3.

Thus precursor1 SMILES: CC(=O)C(F)(F)F

Fragment B (alkene fragment): [C:8]/[CH;D2;+0:9]=[C;H0;D3;+0:10](/[C;D1;H3:11])-[c:12]

Mapping: C8 is attached to CH (C9) which is double bonded to C10 which has a methyl (C11) and attached to aromatic c12. So fragment is something like R-CH= C(CH3)-Ar where R is C8 (maybe a phenyl?). Actually C8 is attached to the rest of molecule? In product side, C8 is a carbon attached to the rest of the molecule (maybe a phenyl). In our target, the aromatic ring is attached to the alkene carbon (C2). The fragment likely is something like phenyl-CH= C(CH3)-Ph? Wait.

Our target: [CH2]=[C]([c]1... ) ... So the alkene carbon is CH2 (C1) double bonded to C2 which is attached to aromatic ring and to the rest of molecule (the cyclobutane). In template, the alkene fragment has a methyl substituent on the double bond (C11). Our target lacks that methyl. So the precursor B would be a methyl-substituted alkene: something like (phenyl)CH= C(CH3)-? Actually C8 is attached to CH (C9) which is double bonded to C10 (which has a methyl C11) and attached to aromatic c12. So the fragment is something like R-CH= C(CH3)-Ar. In our target, R is maybe nothing (hydrogen) because CH2? Actually our target's CH2 is at C1, which is attached to C2 (the double bond). So C1 is CH2, not CH attached to something else. So the precursor B would have CH (C9) attached to something (C8) which could be hydrogen? But C8 is a carbon, maybe a methyl? Could be CH3-CH= C(CH3)-Ar (i.e., 2-methyl-1-phenylpropene). That would be isopropenyl phenyl? Actually CH3-CH= C(CH3)-Ph is 2-methyl-1-phenylprop-1-ene (isopropenylbenzene). That's alpha-methylstyrene. Our target is CH2= C(Ph)-... So it's styrene derivative lacking the methyl. So the template adds a methyl group to the alkene. So retrosynthetically, we can think of target derived from alpha-methylstyrene via demethylation (e.g., oxidative cleavage). But we only need to propose the retrosynthetic step using the template, which splits target into two fragments: the carbonyl fragment (trifluoroacetone) and the alkene fragment (alpha-methylstyrene). However the target does not have the methyl, but the template expects it. So maybe the template can still apply if the methyl is considered as part of the cyclobutane? Wait the cyclobutane part is attached to C2, not to the alkene fragment. The methyl in the template is attached to the alkene carbon that also attaches to the cyclobutane? Actually in template, the alkene fragment includes C8 attached to CH (C9) which is double bonded to C10 (which has methyl C11) and attached to aromatic c12. In target, the cyclobutane attaches to C2 (the double bond carbon). In template, the cyclobutane attaches to C8? Let's examine left side of retro template: [C:8]-[C@@H:9]...-[C@;...:2]... So C8 is attached to C9 (the chiral carbon) which is attached to the cyclobutane (C2). So C8 is the carbon that will become the alkene fragment after cleavage. In target, the carbon attached to cyclobutane is the alkene carbon (C2) which is attached to aromatic ring and double bond to CH2. So C8 corresponds to aromatic carbon? Actually C8 is a carbon attached to the cyclobutane and to the alkene fragment. In target, that carbon is the aromatic carbon? Wait the aromatic ring is attached to C2, not to a separate carbon. So maybe C8 is the aromatic carbon that is part of the phenyl ring? The template may be for a benzylic cleavage.

Given complexity, but we can still propose the precursors as per template: precursor A: CC(=O)C(F)(F)F ; precursor B: Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C (alpha-methylstyrene). Let's write SMILES for alpha-methylstyrene: Cc1ccccc1C=C(C)C? Actually alpha-methylstyrene is Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C? Wait structure: phenyl attached to CH= C(CH3)2? No that's isopropenylbenzene: Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C . That's correct: phenyl-CH= C(CH3)H? Actually isopropenylbenzene: Cc1ccccc1C=CH2? No that's prop-1-enylbenzene. Let's just use SMILES: Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C . That is 1-phenyl-2-methylprop-1-ene? Might be okay.

But we need to ensure mapping: The fragment should have a carbon attached to aromatic (c) and double bond to CH (C9) which is attached to C8 (maybe a methyl). So maybe SMILES: Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C . That has a phenyl attached to C which is double bonded to C which has a methyl. That's fine.

Thus route: target -> reaction (template 1914384) -> precursors: CC(=O)C(F)(F)F and Cc1ccccc1C(=C)C

We need to verify that applying the template forward (i.e., combine these precursors) yields target. Use verify_step.

Let's call verify_step with target SMILES, template_id, precursors list.
